previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, with a history of chronic pancreatitis, distal pancreatectomy, and intestinal malabsorption. Initial concern was for acute pancreatitis, but lipase levels were normal. Imaging showed no gallstones or obstruction, though significant stool burden was noted. Symptoms were attributed to chronic pancreatitis and malabsorption, exacerbated by inconsistent pancreatic enzyme use and opioid-induced constipation. Pain and nausea were managed with Dilaudid and antiemetics, with improvement on IV fluids and dietary support. Her tachycardia and hypotension resolved with hydration. She was discharged with optimized enzyme therapy, dietary recommendations, and follow-up plans with GI and cardiology.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with chronic abdominal pain, now with right
upper quadrant discomfort.

COMPARISON:  CT ___ ultrasound ___.

LIVER/GALLBLADDER ULTRASOUND:

Gray-scale and color Doppler sonographic images demonstrate the liver to be of
normal echotexture and echogenicity with the normal contour.  No focal hepatic
lesion is demonstrated.  There is no ascites.  Main portal venous flow is
hepatopetal.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic bile duct dilatation with
the common bile duct measuring 2 mm. The gallbladder is normal.  There is no
cholelithiasis or "sludge."  There is no pericholecystic fluid or gallbladder
wall thickening.  Limited views of the right kidney are normal.

IMPRESSION:  Unremarkable ultrasound.  Normal gallbladder with no
cholelithiasis or "sludge."
